ABS-CBN is one of the Philippines' largest media and entertainment groups, based in the Manila area and founded in 1946. Revenue comes from advertising, content licensing, subscriptions and international sales to the Filipino diaspora. Its free-to-air broadcast franchise was not renewed in 2020, which cut its reach, though it remains listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange. Very strong consumer recognition across the Philippines, and it reaches Filipinos worldwide.

Advantage Energy is a Calgary-based natural gas producer listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AAV). Its production comes mainly from the liquids-rich Montney formation in northeast Alberta, processed through its Glacier gas plant, and it sells gas and natural gas liquids to Canadian and US markets. A subsidiary, Entropy, develops carbon capture projects. Customers are energy marketers and utilities, so revenue tracks commodity prices. It is a mid-sized Canadian independent with a few hundred million dollars in annual revenue. B2B and resource-sector business with little consumer brand awareness.

Ahli Bank is a commercial bank in Oman, headquartered in Muscat area (Matrah), founded in 1997 and listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange. It offers retail banking, personal and auto loans, credit cards, SME and corporate banking, and Islamic-style financing windows, and earns from lending margins and fees. It is a mid-sized domestic bank competing with Bank Muscat, Sohar International and National Bank of Oman. Customers are Omani individuals and businesses. A regional consumer-facing bank with moderate local brand recognition, sponsorship-active locally, but not a global brand.

Aker Horizons is an Oslo-listed investment company in the Aker group, led by Kjell Inge Rokke, built to develop renewable energy and green industry. Its holdings have included Mainstream Renewable Power, an onshore and offshore wind and solar developer, Aker Offshore Wind, Aker Carbon Capture (later transferred into a joint venture with SLB) and green hydrogen and ammonia plans in Narvik. It earns through development gains and asset sales rather than product sales, and has been reshaped through restructuring since 2023. Based at Fornebu near Oslo. B2B and investor focus, low public brand awareness.

Baijiayun is a Beijing-based provider of cloud video and live-streaming technology. Its platform offers real-time audio and video, online classroom tools and live-broadcast software that enterprises, online education firms and training providers embed into their own apps. Revenue comes from software subscriptions, usage-based cloud services and customised deployments, mostly from Chinese business customers. It is a public company, with most funding raised at an earlier stage. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand visibility, so limited sponsorship appeal beyond China.

Banco de Chile is one of Chile's largest private banks, based in Santiago and founded in 1893. It serves retail customers, SMEs, corporates and wealth clients through a nationwide branch and digital network, with products from mortgages and credit cards to treasury, trade finance and insurance brokerage. It is controlled by the Luksic family's Quinenco group and listed in Santiago and on the NYSE (BCH). Its brand is widely recognised across Chile and it has a long history of sponsoring sport, art and culture locally.

Chemring is a UK-listed (London Stock Exchange: CHG) defence and security company based in Romsey, Hampshire. It makes countermeasure flares and decoys for aircraft and ships, energetic materials, ammunition components and sensors and software, including the Roke security consultancy business. Customers are armed forces and primes, mainly the UK, US and allied governments. It employs roughly 2,000 to 3,000 people, with sites in the UK, US, Norway and Australia, and annual revenue of several hundred million pounds. B2B and government supplier, with little consumer visibility.

CIM Commercial Trust, renamed Creative Media and Community Trust Corporation (CMCT) in 2020, is a Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust listed on Nasdaq and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It owns office buildings, notably in Oakland, Sacramento and Austin, a hotel in Waikiki and multifamily assets, and earns from rent and hospitality. It once also operated a lending business. Customers are commercial tenants and hotel guests. A small-cap landlord with limited public brand awareness.

CSB Bank, formerly the Catholic Syrian Bank, is an Indian private-sector bank headquartered in Thrissur, Kerala, founded in 1920. It offers retail, SME, agri and gold loans, deposits, and NRI services through several hundred branches mainly in South India. Canadian group Fairfax Financial took control in 2018, and the bank listed on the NSE and BSE in December 2019 (CSBBANK). Strong regional recognition in Kerala, but a mid-sized lender with limited national brand profile.

Eagle Point Credit Management is an investment adviser based in Greenwich, Connecticut, that manages closed-end funds and private funds focused on collateralised loan obligation (CLO) equity and junior debt. Its best-known vehicles are Eagle Point Credit Company (NYSE: ECC) and Eagle Point Income Company, which pay regular distributions to retail and institutional investors. It earns management and incentive fees on several billion dollars of assets. Part of the Eagle Point group of credit managers. Finance sector firm with low public brand awareness.

Enphase Energy is a US clean energy technology company, headquartered in Fremont, California, and listed on Nasdaq (ENPH). It pioneered microinverters for solar panels and now sells IQ microinverters, IQ batteries, EV chargers and its Enlighten software, mainly to residential solar installers and distributors in the US, Europe and beyond. It has shipped well over 70 million microinverters and posted revenue above $2 billion in 2023, before a cooldown in rooftop solar demand. Founded in 2006. Strong B2B2C brand in solar, modest direct consumer awareness.

Flushing Bank is the banking arm of Flushing Financial Corporation (Nasdaq: FFIC), headquartered in Uniondale, New York, and founded in 1929. It runs about two dozen branches across Queens, Brooklyn, Manhattan and Long Island, plus an online bank, offering commercial real estate, multifamily and business loans, deposits and cash management. It has around $8 billion in assets and acquired Empire Bancorp in 2021. Regional community bank with local brand recognition in the New York metro area.

Forum Energy Technologies is a Houston-based manufacturer of products for the oil and gas industry, listed on the NYSE (FET). It makes drilling and downhole consumables, coiled tubing, wireline and subsea equipment, valves and pressure-control gear, and is expanding into other industrial and electrification markets. Customers are oilfield service companies, operators and drilling contractors worldwide, with revenue of roughly $700 million to $800 million a year. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer visibility, though a potential corporate hospitality client in the oil and gas sector.

Freehold Royalties is a Calgary-based oil and gas royalty company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (FRU). It owns mineral title and royalty interests across Canada and, more recently, the United States, and receives a share of production revenue from the operators who drill on its lands, without bearing drilling costs. It pays out much of its cash flow as monthly dividends. Revenue depends on oil and gas prices and operator activity. Investor-oriented, B2B business with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

Golden Energy Offshore is a Norwegian offshore shipping company based in Alesund, on Norway's west coast, a hub of the offshore vessel industry. It was set up to own and operate platform supply vessels serving oil and gas platforms in the North Sea and other regions, with charterers being oil companies and offshore operators. It was listed in Oslo as a small shipping company. Crunchbase shows funding of about $95 million in 2025. B2B shipping business with very low public brand awareness.

Golomt Bank is one of Mongolia's largest commercial banks, based in the capital, Ulaanbaatar, and founded in 1995. It offers retail, SME and corporate banking, cards, mobile and internet banking, trade finance and treasury services, and is listed on the Mongolian Stock Exchange. Customers are Mongolian individuals and companies, and it has been active in mining-linked finance and international development funding. Crunchbase shows recent funding of around $114 million. Well known in Mongolia as a consumer bank, but with no international presence.

GreenVolt is a Portuguese renewable energy group based in Lisbon and listed on Euronext Lisbon. It was created from the energy arm of the pulp and paper group Altri, with biomass power plants in Portugal, and expanded into solar, wind and distributed generation in Europe, including the 2022 purchase of Ventient Energy. KKR took a large stake in 2022. It sells electricity to grids and corporate buyers under long-term contracts. Tens of millions of euros in funding are shown. B2B energy producer with low consumer brand awareness.

Guangzhou Zhiguang Electric is a Chinese electrical equipment maker in Guangzhou, listed on the Shenzhen exchange. It makes medium-voltage drives, power quality and reactive power equipment, and grid-side and industrial energy storage systems, selling to utilities, steel, mining, petrochemical and other heavy-industry customers in China. Crunchbase shows funding of about CN 700 million yuan in 2024. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand visibility.

Jordan Kuwait Bank is a commercial bank headquartered in Amman, Jordan, founded in 1976 and listed on the Amman Stock Exchange. It offers retail, corporate, SME and treasury services, cards and digital banking through a network of branches in Jordan and Cyprus. Burgan Bank, part of Kuwait's KIPCO group, is a major shareholder. Crunchbase shows funding of around $100 million in 2026. A mid-sized Jordanian bank with solid domestic brand recognition.

Karnataka Bank is an Indian private-sector bank based in Mangalore, founded in 1924 and listed on the NSE and BSE. It runs roughly 900 branches, with a concentration in Karnataka and a presence in other states, serving retail, agricultural, MSME and corporate customers with deposits, loans, cards and digital banking. Total business is above 1.5 trillion rupees. It is a well-known regional lender in coastal Karnataka, with limited national profile compared with larger Indian banks.

Korea Gas Corporation (KOGAS) is South Korea's state-controlled importer and wholesaler of liquefied natural gas, among the largest LNG buyers in the world. It operates the national gas pipeline network and LNG receiving terminals, and sells gas to power generators and city-gas distributors, with overseas upstream and LNG projects. Its headquarters were moved to Daegu, and it is listed on the Korea Exchange. Revenue runs to tens of billions of dollars. B2B utility supplier, with low consumer visibility inside Korea.

Malibu Life Re is a financial services and insurance company based in George Town, Cayman Islands, and flagged in the data as a listed (public) company. It has a modest branch network and a strong digital and cards focus. Customers are urban Sri Lankan individuals and mid-sized companies. Recognised consumer brand domestically, but a mid-sized bank without an international presence.

Performance Shipping is a Greek tanker company based in Athens and listed on Nasdaq (PSHG). It was spun out of Aegean Shipping interests and Crunchbase shows funding of about $100 million. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars, driven by tanker rates. B2B shipping company with no consumer brand profile.

Sekerbank is a Turkish private commercial bank based in Istanbul, founded in 1953 by sugar beet farmers' cooperatives and listed on Borsa Istanbul (SKBNK). It serves small and medium businesses, farmers and retail customers with lending, deposits, cards and trade finance across a network of a few hundred branches. Its roots in agriculture and SME banking set it apart from larger Turkish banks. Crunchbase shows funding of around $118 million in 2025. Recognised domestic consumer bank, mid-sized and Turkey-focused.

Shanghai Lingang Economic Development Group is a state-backed developer of industrial parks and the Lingang area of Shanghai, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It develops and operates industrial land, science and technology parks, commercial property and related financial and investment holdings, and benefits from government-led development of the Lingang free-trade zone. Customers are tenant companies and industrial investors. Funding of around CN 800 million yuan is shown for 2024. B2B and state-linked, with little consumer visibility.

Sigenergy is a Shanghai-based energy technology company founded in 2022 that makes home and commercial energy storage and solar systems. Its products include the SigenStor all-in-one battery and inverter, SigenStar hybrid inverters and EV chargers, managed through an app and AI-based energy management software. It sells through installers and distributors in Europe, Australia, Asia and other regions. Crunchbase shows funding of about CN 710 million yuan in 2024. Growing brand in home solar and storage, mainly known to installers rather than consumers.

Societe Generale is one of France's largest banks, founded in 1864 and headquartered in Paris. It operates retail banking in France through SG and Boursorama, international retail units including KB in the Czech Republic and BRD in Romania, car leasing and fleet management through Ayvens, plus global investment banking, markets and asset servicing. It has well over 100,000 employees and is listed on Euronext Paris. A long-time sports and cultural sponsor, with strong brand recognition in Europe and Africa.

Tamar Petroleum is an Israeli company, based in Herzliya, that holds a 16.75% interest in the Tamar offshore natural gas field in the Eastern Mediterranean. Revenue comes from selling gas to Israeli power producers, industry and exports, under long-term contracts, with the field operated by Chevron. It is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TMRP) after a 2017 public bond and share offering. It has a handful of staff and is financed largely through bonds. Investor-oriented asset company with no consumer brand profile.

UBA Group, formally United Bank for Africa, is a pan-African banking group headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, founded in 1949 and listed on the Nigerian Exchange. It serves tens of millions of customers through subsidiaries in around 20 African countries, with offices in the UK, US and France, offering retail, corporate, trade finance, cards and payments. Tony Elumelu's Heirs Holdings is a major shareholder. A leading consumer banking brand across Africa and a regular sponsor of sport, music and charity in the region.

AAON is a US maker of heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment, headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and listed on Nasdaq. It builds rooftop units, heat pumps, chillers, air handlers and coils for commercial and industrial buildings, increasingly for data centres, selling through independent representatives to contractors and building owners. Founded in 1988, it has revenue of well over $1 billion and plants in Oklahoma and Texas. B2B manufacturer with low consumer brand awareness.

Bonheur is a Norwegian holding company controlled by the Fred. Olsen family, based in Oslo and listed on Oslo Bors. Its businesses include Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines, plus other marine and energy holdings. The Fred. Olsen name goes back to 1848. Revenue comes from power sales, charters and cruise holidays. The cruise line has consumer brand recognition in the UK.

Canaccord Genuity Group is an independent financial services firm, with roots in Vancouver and Toronto, offering wealth management and capital markets services. Its wealth arm operates in Canada, the UK and Crown Dependencies, and Australia, while the capital markets arm provides investment banking, research and trading for growth companies in technology, mining, healthcare and other sectors, in North America, the UK and Europe, and Asia. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (CF) and founded in 1950. Revenue is above C$1.5 billion. Known mainly to investors and companies.

CashPlus is a Moroccan financial services and payments company based in Casablanca, listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. It operates a large network of agents and shops across Morocco offering money transfers, bill payments, cash services, prepaid cards and mobile wallets, serving mostly unbanked and under-banked consumers as well as migrant workers sending money home. It earns fees on transactions. Crunchbase shows funding of about $67 million. A recognised consumer-facing financial brand in Morocco.

Cohen and Steers is a New York-based asset manager specialising in real assets and alternative income, including listed real estate securities, infrastructure, commodities and preferred securities. Founded in 1986, it manages roughly $80 billion to $90 billion for institutional and retail investors through mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts. It is listed on the NYSE (CNS). Revenue comes from management fees. Well known among financial professionals, with little public brand awareness.

Digital China is a Beijing-based information technology services company that came out of Legend Holdings, with listed entities in Hong Kong and Shenzhen. It distributes IT hardware and software, builds systems for government and enterprises, and offers cloud, smart city and IT outsourcing services, serving banks, telecom operators, government and corporate clients across China. Crunchbase shows a funding round dated 2008. B2B technology integrator with little consumer brand visibility.

Huami, renamed Zepp Health in 2021, is a Chinese wearables company, founded in 2013 with a Beijing base and large operations in Hefei. Customers are consumers worldwide via Amazon, retailers and its own stores, and it is listed on the NYSE (ZEPP). Revenue is a few hundred million dollars. Amazfit has solid consumer recognition, with sponsorship activity in sports.

Mid Penn Bank is the community bank of Mid Penn Bancorp (Nasdaq: MPB), headquartered in Millersburg, Pennsylvania. It offers commercial lending, retail banking, wealth management and mortgage services through roughly 50 to 60 branches in central and eastern Pennsylvania and nearby states, with total assets around $5 billion to $6 billion after acquisitions such as Brunswick Bancorp in 2023. Regional bank with local brand recognition and community sponsorships, no national consumer profile.

NSIA Bank is a commercial bank based in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, part of the NSIA Group, a West African financial group that also includes insurance. It serves retail customers, small businesses and corporates with accounts, loans, cards and trade finance, and operates in several francophone West African countries. The group is regionally listed and Crunchbase shows funding of about $79 million in 2026. A recognised regional financial brand in French-speaking West Africa.

Pieridae Energy is a Calgary-based Canadian natural gas company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (PEA). It produces natural gas and liquids from the Alberta foothills and processes it at its Caroline and Brazeau plants, selling to North American markets. It is better known for its long-planned Goldboro LNG export project in Nova Scotia, aimed at supplying European buyers. Funding shown is around C$101 million in 2024. B2B resource company with essentially no consumer visibility.

Pyxis Tankers is a Greek shipping company with offices in Maroussi, Athens, listed on Nasdaq (PXS). It owns a small fleet of medium range product tankers that carry refined petroleum products and chemicals for oil majors and traders, and was founded in 2007 under Valentios Valentis. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars. Crunchbase shows funding of about $60 million. B2B shipping company with very little public brand awareness.

Quest Resource Holding Corporation is a Frisco, Texas-based environmental services company listed on Nasdaq (QRHC). It manages waste and recycling for businesses with many sites, such as retailers, restaurants and automotive centres, arranging pickup, processing and reporting, and earns revenue from service fees and recycling. Customers include national brands and facilities across the US. Revenue is roughly $280 million per year. B2B services firm with little consumer visibility.

Royal Helium is a Canadian exploration and development company based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. It explores for helium, and sometimes associated gases, in southern Saskatchewan and Alberta, and has worked on processing and production facilities such as the Climax and Steveville projects. Potential customers are industrial gas companies selling helium to medical, electronics and scientific users. Funding of about $84 million is shown. Resource company with no consumer brand visibility.

Suez Canal Bank is an Egyptian commercial bank based in Cairo, founded in 1978, with shares traded on the Egyptian Exchange. It serves retail, SME and corporate customers with accounts, loans, cards and trade services through a branch network in Egypt, including the Suez Canal region. It is a mid-sized domestic bank with a government-linked shareholder base. Crunchbase shows funding of around $61 million in 2026. Known locally as a retail bank, without an international brand.

Unibank is a commercial bank in Armenia, headquartered in Yerevan, founded in the early 1990s. It offers retail banking, loans and cards, SME and corporate services, and digital banking in Armenia, with customers who are mainly Armenian households and businesses. Crunchbase shows funding of about $72 million in 2026. A mid-sized domestic lender with local brand recognition, and a possible local sponsor, but without any international presence.

It also develops carbon products for other uses. Customers are utilities, municipalities and industrial companies, and revenue is under $200 million a year. Crunchbase shows funding of about $55 million. B2B materials company with no consumer brand awareness.

A clinical-stage biotech with no revenue and no consumer brand visibility.

Bank Alfalah is one of Pakistan's largest private commercial banks, based in Karachi and listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (BAFL). Strong consumer brand in Pakistan, and an active sponsor of sports, notably cricket, and cultural events.

Brilliant Earth is a US jewellery retailer based in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (BRLT), founded in 2005. It sells engagement rings, wedding bands and fine jewellery with a focus on ethically sourced diamonds, lab-grown diamonds, recycled precious metals and customised designs, mainly via its website and about 40 to 50 showrooms across the US, plus the UK and Canada. Customers are consumers, especially engaged couples. Revenue is roughly $400 million to $450 million. Known direct-to-consumer brand in bridal jewellery.

Cohort is a UK defence and security technology group, based in Theale, Berkshire, and listed on AIM (CHRT). Customers are the UK Ministry of Defence, NATO nations and export markets. Revenue is above 200 million pounds. B2B defence contractor with little public brand profile, though recent defence spending has lifted its profile with investors.

Community Heritage Financial is a US bank holding company for a community bank, with its base in the town of Middletown. It offers deposits, residential and commercial loans and personal banking to local households and small businesses through a handful of branches. Crunchbase shows a funding amount of about $38.5 million, dated late 2024. A small regional bank with local brand recognition only.

DFCC Bank is a Sri Lankan bank based in Colombo, founded in 1955 as a development finance institution and converted to a commercial bank. It has a mid-sized network of branches and a growing digital offer. Crunchbase shows funding of about $56 million in early 2026. Recognised Sri Lankan bank brand, domestic focus.

EchoStar is a US satellite and wireless company based in Englewood, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (SATS). Its Hughes unit sells HughesNet satellite internet and network equipment for consumers, enterprises and governments. It merged with Dish Network in December 2023, adding Boost Mobile, Sling TV and a 5G network build, and in 2025 agreed to sell spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX. Founded by Charlie Ergen, it has revenue of around $15 billion. Boost Mobile and Sling are recognised US consumer brands.

Enservco is a Denver-based oilfield services company listed on NYSE American, providing hot oiling, frac water heating, acidizing and well-site support to oil and gas producers, mainly in the Rockies, Texas and Appalachia. It also developed a clean-heat technology offering. B2B niche service provider with no consumer brand visibility.

HydrogenPro is a Norwegian maker of large-scale alkaline water electrolysers for green hydrogen production, based in Porsgrunn and listed on Euronext Oslo. Revenue comes from advertising, events and licensing, and its audiences are urban and Hispanic listeners in New York, Los Angeles and other markets. Strong brand recognition in urban radio, with live events such as Summer Jam.

National Development Bank (NDB) is a Sri Lankan commercial bank based in Colombo, founded in 1979 as a development finance institution and now listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange. Crunchbase shows funding of around LKR 16 billion in 2026. Recognised domestic brand, with a track record of local sponsorships.

Novatti Group is an Australian payments and fintech company based in Melbourne and listed on the ASX (NOV). It provides payment processing, prepaid and card programs, remittance and cross-border transfers, and offers licensed payment services to businesses, banks and government clients. It has grown by acquisition and has a small revenue base. Funding of about $40 million is shown. B2B financial technology brand, with little consumer awareness.

Peoples Bancorp is a US bank holding company headquartered in Marietta, Ohio, and listed on Nasdaq (PEBO). It has roughly $9 billion in assets, growing through acquisitions such as Limestone Bancorp in 2022. Regional community bank with good local recognition and community sponsorships.

Stockwik Forvaltning is a Swedish company based in Stockholm, listed on Nasdaq First North, that acquires and develops small and medium-sized Swedish businesses, mostly in niches such as services, trade and industry. It aims to be a long-term owner of unlisted companies, earning revenue from subsidiaries and dividends. It has raised several hundred million kronor, with SEK 426 million shown. Investor-oriented holding company with no consumer brand awareness.

UGE is a New York-based developer of solar and distributed energy systems, listed on the Toronto Venture Exchange. It designs, builds and owns solar projects, including community solar, rooftop and on-site systems for municipalities, commercial building owners and utilities in North America and emerging markets, and also develops energy storage. Funding of about $47 million is shown. B2B renewable energy contractor with little public brand awareness.

United Finance is a finance and leasing company based in Muscat, Oman, listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange. It provides vehicle and equipment leasing, consumer and business loans, and deposits-like products to individuals and small firms, regulated by the Central Bank of Oman. It is smaller than the main Omani banks. Funding of about OMR 15 million is shown for 2025. Local brand with moderate recognition in Oman.

Verde Clean Fuels is a Houston-based clean fuels developer listed on Nasdaq (VGAS) after a 2023 SPAC merger. It owns the STG+ process, which converts syngas from natural gas, biomass or waste into gasoline-grade fuel, and plans plants that turn feedstock into low-carbon gasoline blendstock. It has no commercial plant yet and is pre-revenue. Customers would be refiners and fuel distributors. Funding of about $50 million is shown. Development-stage energy technology company with no consumer visibility.

Washington Trust is the parent of The Washington Trust Company, a bank headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island, which claims to be the oldest community bank in the US, founded in 1800, and is listed on Nasdaq (WASH). It offers commercial banking, mortgages and wealth management, with about $7 billion in assets and branches across Rhode Island and Connecticut and Massachusetts. Strong regional brand in New England, with a visible community sponsorship record.

AG Mortgage Investment Trust is a New York-based mortgage real estate investment trust listed on the NYSE (MITT). It invests in residential mortgage assets, including non-agency loans, agency securities and credit-sensitive securities, financed with repurchase agreements. It is externally managed by Angelo Gordon, which TPG acquired in 2023, and pays dividends from net interest income. Investors are mainly institutions and income-seeking retail shareholders. No consumer brand profile.

Alandsbanken is a bank based in Mariehamn on the Aland Islands, Finland, listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, founded in 1919. It offers private banking, wealth management, mortgages and business banking in Aland, mainland Finland and Sweden, plus technology services through its Crosskey subsidiary for banks. It is small, with total assets of around 5 billion euros. Funding of SEK 350 million is shown. Known locally and in Nordic private banking, without a wider consumer profile.

AIM Industrial Growth Freehold and Leasehold REIT is a Thai real estate investment trust based in Bangkok and listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. It owns and leases warehouses, factories and logistics space to industrial and logistics tenants, and distributes rental income to unit holders. Capital raised is shown as THB 1.1 billion in 2025. Investors are mostly Thai institutions and retail unit holders. Investment vehicle with no consumer brand.

Alternergy is a Philippine renewable energy developer based in Makati, listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange. It develops wind, solar and hydro projects, including the Alabat Wind Power Project in Quezon and the Tanay Wind Power Project in Rizal, selling electricity to the grid and to commercial customers. It raised about 2 billion pesos in 2026. Customers are utilities and industrial energy buyers. B2B renewable power company with limited public brand awareness.

Aquarius Engines is an Israeli engine technology company listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It develops and commercialises a lightweight free-piston engine that uses a linear motion design with few moving parts, designed for use in generators, range extenders and other applications, as a low-emission alternative to conventional engines. It is an early stage company. Funding of about $29 million is shown for 2025. Prospective customers are engine and equipment makers; there is no consumer visibility.

Asia Dragon Trust is a UK investment trust based in Edinburgh and listed on the London Stock Exchange, managed by abrdn. It invests in a portfolio of Asia-Pacific equities, excluding Japan, seeking long-term capital growth for private and institutional investors. It was formed from the combination of Asian trusts earlier this decade and has assets of several hundred million pounds. Shareholders buy shares via brokers and platforms. No consumer brand visibility beyond the investment trust market.

Bank Capital Indonesia is a commercial bank based in Jakarta, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BACA). It offers savings and deposits, loans to small businesses and individuals, and treasury services, and is a smaller bank in Indonesia's market. It raised about IDR 470 billion in a 2025 capital increase. Customers are Indonesian retail and SME clients. Moderate regional recognition, not a leading consumer brand.

Bank Nationalnobu, trading as Nobu Bank, is an Indonesian bank based in Tangerang, Banten, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (NOBU). It provides retail and SME banking, deposits, loans and increasingly digital banking in Indonesia. It is a small to mid-sized lender with a focus on the greater Jakarta area. Funding of about IDR 560 billion is shown, dated mid-2025. Local brand with modest recognition in Indonesia.

ChoiceOne Bank is the subsidiary of ChoiceOne Financial Services, a bank holding company listed on Nasdaq (COFS) and based in Sparta, Michigan. The bank offers commercial and consumer lending, deposits, trust and wealth management through branches across western and central Michigan, and has grown by acquisition, with roughly $2.5 billion to $3 billion in assets. Funding of about $34.5 million is shown, dated 2024. Regional community bank with local brand recognition.

Faysal Bank is a Pakistani bank based in Karachi, listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange, which converted to a full Islamic bank. It offers retail, SME, corporate and consumer finance, cards, and Islamic banking services through a few hundred branches nationwide. It is a mid-sized Pakistani bank with deposits in the hundreds of billions of rupees. Funding of PKR 7 billion is shown for 2026. Known consumer financial brand in Pakistan.

Femto Technologies is a company based in Qiryat Bialik, Israel, flagged as listed. Crunchbase tags it with asset management and CRM, but gives no description, so its products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. Funding of about $26.6 million is shown, dated February 2025. The tags are inconsistent with each other, so the real business line is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

First Capital Bank is a bank based in Charleston, South Carolina, in the United States, flagged as listed and tagged in Crunchbase under banking and commercial lending. No description is available, so its size, branch network and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. Funding of about $34.1 million is shown, dated May 2024, which points to a capital raise. It is likely a small regional commercial bank. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Gulf Oil Lubricants India is the Indian arm of the Hinduja Group's Gulf Oil brand, based in Mumbai and listed on the NSE and BSE. It makes and markets automotive and industrial lubricants, greases and coolants, including Gulf Pride, Gulf Oil Premium and Gulf Formula, through distributors, workshops and retail outlets across India. Customers are motorists, fleet operators and industries. Revenue is about 3,000 crore rupees a year. Gulf is a well-known brand in India with a history of sports sponsorship, including cricket and motorsport.

Halmont Properties Corporation is a real estate and asset management company based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, flagged as listed. Crunchbase tags it with asset management and finance, and provides no description, so its property types, tenants and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. Funding of about C$50 million is shown, dated end of 2024. It is likely a smaller Canadian property owner. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Lasaco Assurance is a Nigerian general insurance company based in Ikeja, Lagos, listed on the Nigerian Exchange. It writes motor, fire, marine, engineering, accident and other non-life insurance policies for individuals and companies. It is a long-established mid-sized insurer, with a recapitalisation to meet new regulatory capital rules reflected in funding of about 48.5 billion naira shown for late 2026. Known in the Nigerian insurance market, with limited consumer brand awareness.

MPC Energy Solutions is a Dutch-registered renewable energy investment company, with offices in Amsterdam, listed on Euronext Oslo, and affiliated with Hamburg-based MPC Capital. It invests in and operates solar, hydro and other clean power projects in emerging markets, selling electricity under long-term contracts. Funding of about $34 million is shown, dated 2024. Customers are utilities and commercial buyers. Investor-oriented company with little consumer brand visibility.

Norwood Financial is the bank holding company for Wayne Bank, headquartered in Honesdale, Pennsylvania, and listed on Nasdaq (NWFL). It offers commercial and retail banking, mortgages and wealth management across northeastern Pennsylvania and the New York Southern Tier and Hudson Valley, with about $2.2 billion in assets. Funding of $26 million is shown, dated December 2024. Regional community bank with local brand recognition, no national profile.

One Bank is a private commercial bank in Bangladesh, based in Dhaka and listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange. It provides retail, SME and corporate banking, cards, remittance and digital banking services through a network of branches. It is a mid-sized bank. Crunchbase shows a capital raise of BDT 4 billion in 2026. A domestic financial brand with moderate recognition in Bangladesh.

PRYME is a Dutch advanced plastic recycling company based in Rotterdam and listed on Euronext Growth Oslo. It uses pyrolysis technology to turn mixed plastic waste into pyrolysis oil used as feedstock for new plastics and fuels, operating a plant in the Port of Rotterdam region. Customers are chemical and refining companies. It is an early commercial stage business with large capital needs, and about 28 million is shown in funding. B2B cleantech firm with little consumer brand awareness.

Rapala VMC is a Finnish fishing tackle group based in Helsinki, famous for the Rapala floating lure invented by Lauri Rapala in 1936. Its brands include Rapala, Storm, Sufix, VMC hooks, Luhr-Jensen, Marttiini knives and Blue Fox, sold in over 100 countries through sports retailers and fishing stores. Customers are recreational anglers. It was listed on Nasdaq Helsinki and has revenue of about 250 million euros. Very recognisable among anglers, a strong niche consumer brand with sponsored fishing professionals.

Sound Energy is a UK-based upstream gas company listed on AIM, with offices in London. Its main asset is the Tendrara gas concession in eastern Morocco, where it is developing a gas-to-power and LNG supply project to serve Moroccan industrial customers. It is a development-stage business, funded by equity raises, with revenue still small. Funding of about $31 million is shown for 2024. B2B energy explorer with no consumer brand visibility.

Tallinna Vesi is the water and wastewater utility of the Estonian capital Tallinn, listed on Nasdaq Tallinn. Under a long-term concession it supplies drinking water and treats wastewater for more than 400,000 customers, earning regulated tariffs. Utilitas, an Estonian energy group, is its largest shareholder, after previously being controlled by United Utilities and then Veolia. Revenue is about 70 million euros. Well known in Estonia as a utility, with low consumer brand marketing.

Unimech Aerospace is an Indian precision engineering company based in Bengaluru, listed on the NSE and BSE after its late 2024 IPO. It makes high-precision machined components, tooling and assemblies for aerospace and defence customers and other engineering sectors, selling to global aircraft and engine makers. Funding of about 2.5 billion rupees is shown for 2024. Revenue is in the low tens of billions of rupees. B2B manufacturer with little public brand awareness.

Voxeljet is a German 3D printing company based in Friedberg, near Augsburg, listed on Nasdaq (VJET). It builds large-format industrial 3D printers using binder-jetting to make sand moulds and cores for metal casting, plastic parts and prototypes, and also prints parts as a service. Customers are foundries and manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, engineering and art. It has revenue of roughly 30 to 40 million euros and has been loss-making. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

XChange TEC is a Shanghai-based financial technology company in the insurance technology and SaaS space, offering digital platforms used by insurance agents and brokers to sell and manage insurance products in China. It earns fees from software and sales services. Funding of about $25 million is shown, dated September 2024, and it is flagged as listed. Customers are Chinese insurance intermediaries, with no consumer brand awareness outside its channel.

ZlinePay is a Chinese financial technology company based in Chengdu, Sichuan, tagged in Crunchbase under fintech and mobile payment and flagged as listed. No further description is available, so its products, customer base and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. Funding of about CN 213 million yuan is shown, with the date recorded as November 2014. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Amgen is a US biotechnology company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, listed on Nasdaq (AMGN), founded in 1980. It sells biologic medicines including Enbrel, Prolia and Xgeva, Repatha, Otezla, Aranesp and Tezspire, plus biosimilars, and bought Horizon Therapeutics in 2023 for about $28 billion. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems worldwide. Revenue is around $33 billion with roughly 28,000 employees. It is a very large pharma brand, known to doctors and investors more than the general public.

Amicus Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in Princeton, New Jersey, and listed on Nasdaq (FOLD). It specialises in rare metabolic and lysosomal diseases, selling Galafold, an oral treatment for Fabry disease, and Pombiliti plus Opfolda, a combination therapy for late-onset Pompe disease. Customers are specialist physicians, hospitals and patients in the US, Europe, Japan and other markets. Revenue is roughly $500 million to $600 million a year, with total funding of about $2.6 billion. Known mainly to rare-disease doctors and investors, with no consumer brand awareness.

Ascendis Pharma is a Danish biopharmaceutical company based in Hellerup, near Copenhagen, listed on Nasdaq (ASND). It uses its TransCon prodrug technology to create longer-acting versions of drugs, with products including Skytrofa (weekly growth hormone) and Yorvipath (hypoparathyroidism), approved in 2024, and Sanofi-partnered and other programmes in development. Customers are specialist physicians and patients in the US and Europe. Revenue is growing from a low base, with accumulated funding of about $1.9 billion. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

BioCryst Pharmaceuticals is a US biotechnology company based in Durham, North Carolina, and listed on Nasdaq (BCRX). Its main product is Orladeyo (berotralstat), a once-daily oral therapy to prevent attacks in hereditary angioedema, sold in the US, Europe, Japan and other markets, with other rare disease drugs in development. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars a year. Total funding of about $1.8 billion is shown. Known to specialist doctors and rare-disease patients, with no mainstream consumer profile.

Cerevel Therapeutics was a Boston-based clinical-stage neuroscience biotechnology company developing treatments for Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia and epilepsy, led by the Parkinson's candidate tavapadon. It was acquired by AbbVie in August 2024 in a deal valued at about $8.7 billion, and no longer trades independently. Originally launched in 2018 with backing from Bain Capital and Pfizer. It had no commercial products at the time of the sale. B2B pharma development company with no consumer brand profile.

Mirati Therapeutics was a San Diego-based oncology biotechnology company known for Krazati (adagrasib), an oral KRAS G12C inhibitor approved in 2022 for certain lung and colorectal cancers. Bristol Myers Squibb acquired it in January 2024 for about $4.8 billion upfront, so it is now part of BMS. It sold to oncologists and cancer centres in the US, with total funding of about $2.6 billion before the sale. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

PacBio (Pacific Biosciences of California) is a life sciences instrument company based in Menlo Park, California, and listed on Nasdaq (PACB). It makes long-read DNA sequencing systems, notably the Revio and Sequel platforms using HiFi sequencing, and sells instruments, consumables and services to genomics labs, universities, pharma and clinical researchers worldwide. It was founded in 2004 and has revenue of roughly $150 million to $200 million, with losses. Well known among scientists, but no consumer visibility.

Reata Pharmaceuticals was a Plano, Texas biopharmaceutical company that developed Skyclarys (omaveloxolone), the first approved treatment for Friedreich's ataxia, cleared by the FDA in early 2023. Biogen acquired Reata in September 2023 for about $7.3 billion, so it is now part of Biogen. Customers were neurologists and rare disease patients. Total funding was about $2 billion before the acquisition. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand recognition.

Roivant Sciences is a biopharmaceutical holding company, based in New York with a UK origin, listed on Nasdaq (ROIV). It builds subsidiary biotech companies called Vants, including Immunovant (immunology antibodies), Priovant (brepocitinib), and previously Dermavant, whose Vtama cream was sold to Organon, and Telavant, sold to Roche in 2023 for about $7 billion. Founded by Vivek Ramaswamy in 2014. Funding of about $2.5 billion is shown. Known to investors and the biotech industry, not to consumers.

Spirit Realty Capital was a US real estate investment trust, based in Dallas, Texas, that owned about 2,000 single-tenant net lease properties, such as retail, restaurants, convenience stores and industrial sites, leased to many tenants across the US. It was listed on the NYSE (SRC) until Realty Income acquired it in January 2024 in a deal valued at about $9.3 billion. The Zimbabwe location in the input appears to be an error. Property investor with no consumer brand profile.

Bio-Rad Laboratories is a life science research and clinical diagnostics company based in Hercules, California, listed on the NYSE (BIO) and founded in 1952. It makes laboratory instruments and reagents, including Droplet Digital PCR, electrophoresis and imaging systems, plus diagnostic tests for blood typing, diabetes and infectious diseases, sold to hospitals, labs, universities and biopharma worldwide. Revenue is around $2.5 billion to $2.8 billion with about 8,000 employees. B2B brand well known in labs, not among consumers.

Charles River Laboratories is a US contract research organisation based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, and listed on the NYSE (CRL), founded in 1947. It provides preclinical drug discovery and safety testing services, research animal models, and manufacturing support services to pharma and biotech companies, regulators and academic labs in about 20 countries. Revenue is about $4 billion with 20,000 employees. Well known in the pharma industry, with no consumer awareness.

Dow is a US materials science giant based in Midland, Michigan, listed on the NYSE (DOW) since its 2019 spin-off from DowDuPont. It makes plastics such as polyethylene, packaging materials, industrial intermediates, coatings and silicones for packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer-care customers in over 100 countries. Revenue is around $43 billion with about 36,000 employees. B2B maker with strong corporate brand recognition and a long record in major sports sponsorship, including as a worldwide Olympic partner.

Focus Media is China's largest out-of-home advertising network, based in Shanghai and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, led by founder Jiang Nanjun. It operates tens of thousands of digital display screens in apartment building lifts and entrances, plus screens in cinemas and shops, selling advertising slots to consumer brands, with many advertising customers in FMCG, internet and automotive. It was taken private from Nasdaq in 2013 and relisted in China in 2015. Revenue is in the billions of yuan. B2B media business with high advertiser recognition.

Ginkgo Bioworks is a US synthetic biology company based in Boston and listed on the NYSE (DNA), going public through a SPAC merger in 2021. It runs automated cell programming laboratories (foundries) and offers a platform to design and engineer microbes and enzymes for pharma, agriculture, food and industrial customers on a fee and milestone basis. It also provides biosecurity services. Revenue is around $200 million a year, with large losses. Well known in biotech, but not to consumers.

Huntsman is a US specialty chemicals manufacturer based in The Woodlands, Texas, and listed on the NYSE (HUN). It produces polyurethanes such as MDI, performance products, and advanced materials including epoxy and composites for construction, automotive, aerospace, coatings and consumer goods customers in about 25 countries. Revenue is around $6 billion with roughly 6,000 employees. The Huntsman family founded it in 1970. B2B brand with no consumer awareness, although its corporate name is widely recognised in industry.

Immunocore is a UK biotechnology company based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and listed on Nasdaq (IMCR). It develops T cell receptor bispecific immunotherapies, with its approved drug Kimmtrak (tebentafusp) for uveal melanoma, a rare eye cancer, sold in the US and Europe, plus pipeline programmes in other cancers and autoimmune disease. Customers are oncologists and hospitals. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars, with total funding of about $1.2 billion. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Koubei is a Chinese local services and restaurant discovery platform, based in Hangzhou, which started as an Alibaba business and was relaunched in 2015 as a joint venture of Alibaba and Ant Group. It offered consumer reviews, coupons and mobile payment-linked offers for restaurants and local shops, and was later merged with Ele.me into Alibaba's local services business. Customers are Chinese consumers and merchants. It raised about $1.6 billion in funding. Strong brand recognition in China in its time.

Kura Oncology is a US clinical and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (KURA). It develops targeted oral cancer drugs, led by ziftomenib, a menin inhibitor for acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1 mutations, and farnesyl transferase inhibitor tipifarnib. Customers are oncologists and hospitals. It has total funding of about $1.2 billion and is early in commercialisation. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Iovance Biotherapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in San Carlos, California, and listed on Nasdaq (IOVA). It developed Amtagvi (lifileucel), the first tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy, approved by the FDA in February 2024 for advanced melanoma, and is testing it in lung and other cancers. Customers are specialist cancer centres, with each treatment made from a patient's own cells. Revenue is early stage, with funding of about $1.6 billion shown. Known to oncologists and investors only.

New Amsterdam Pharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with Dutch roots, listed on Nasdaq (NAMS), focused on cardiovascular disease. Its lead drug, obicetrapib, is an oral CETP inhibitor designed to lower LDL cholesterol in patients with heart disease or high cholesterol, developed with partner Menarini in Europe. It raised about $1.2 billion in total funding and has no approved product yet. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Oxford Nanopore Technologies is a UK life sciences company based in Oxford and listed on the London Stock Exchange (ONT) since its 2021 IPO. It makes nanopore DNA and RNA sequencing devices, including the pocket-size MinION and the high-throughput PromethION, sold to research labs, public health agencies, pharma and clinical customers, and used in COVID-19 genomic surveillance. Founded in 2005, it has revenue of about 180 to 200 million pounds and is loss-making. Respected in science, with no consumer brand awareness.

Verona Pharma was a UK-founded respiratory biopharmaceutical company, with offices in London and Raleigh, whose product Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine) was approved by the FDA in 2024 as a nebulised maintenance treatment for COPD. It was listed on Nasdaq. Merck agreed to buy Verona in 2025 for around $10 billion, so it is now part of Merck. Customers are pulmonologists, pharmacies and COPD patients in the US. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

Yara International is a Norwegian crop nutrition company based in Oslo and listed on Euronext Oslo, with the Norwegian state as a major shareholder. It is one of the world's largest producers of nitrogen fertilisers and ammonia, along with industrial nitrogen products and digital farming tools, selling in more than 60 countries to farmers, distributors and industry. Revenue is around $14 billion to $15 billion with about 17,000 employees. B2B brand well known in agriculture.

Akero Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, developing efruxifermin, an FGF21 analogue for treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a serious fatty liver disease. It was listed on Nasdaq, and in late 2025 Novo Nordisk agreed to acquire it for a deal worth several billion dollars. It had no approved product or revenue. Funding of about $951 million is shown. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Bicycle Therapeutics is a UK-founded biotechnology company based in Cambridge, listed on Nasdaq (BCYC), with a US office in Lexington, Massachusetts. It develops Bicycle peptide therapeutics, small constrained peptides with antibody-like binding, including toxin conjugates against solid tumours such as zelenectide pevedotin. It earns collaboration revenue from partners such as Genentech, Novartis and Bayer. Total funding of about $1.1 billion is shown. Clinical-stage, with no consumer brand profile.

Essential Pharma is a UK specialty pharmaceutical company based in Egham, Surrey, that acquires, develops and markets established and niche medicines for rare diseases and hospital use across Europe, the Middle East and other markets. It grows by acquiring brands from larger pharma groups and supplying them to hospitals and pharmacies. It is backed by private capital, with funding of about 900 million shown for late 2024. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Establishment Labs is a medical technology company based in Alajuela, Costa Rica, and listed on Nasdaq (ESTA). It makes Motiva breast implants, which use its SmoothSilk surface, plus minimally invasive aesthetic devices, and sells them through surgeons in more than 80 countries, with the US as the key growth market after FDA approval in 2024. Revenue is roughly $160 million to $170 million. Surgeons are the buyers; patients know the Motiva brand in aesthetics but it has low general public awareness.

ETG, formerly Export Trading Group, is a Mauritius-registered agricultural supply chain group that sources, processes and distributes crops, inputs and food staples across Africa and Asia. It operates in about 40 countries in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, buying from farmers and selling inputs, commodities such as rice, pulses and grain, and providing logistics. It is privately held and employs many thousands of people, with revenue in the billions of dollars. B2B commodities and agri-inputs group with little consumer visibility.

Eurofins Scientific is a Luxembourg-based testing and laboratory services group, listed on Euronext Paris and controlled by the Martin family. It runs hundreds of labs in about 60 countries, testing food, environment, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and clinical samples, as well as genomics and diagnostics. Revenue is about 6.5 billion to 7 billion euros with some 60,000 employees. Customers are producers, retailers, pharma and regulators. B2B brand known in industry, not to consumers.

Froy is a Norwegian aquaculture services company known for operating well boats and vessels that serve salmon farmers, with services such as fish transport, delousing, treatment and freight. Crunchbase gives its base as Freya, Sogn og Fjordane, Norway. Customers are fish farming companies along the Norwegian coast. It shows a large funding total of NOK 10.1 billion, dated April 2026, which likely reflects vessel financing. B2B maritime services with no consumer brand profile.

Gentiva is a US home health, hospice and personalised care provider headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, one of the largest hospice operators in the country with hundreds of locations across many states. It provides nursing, therapy and end-of-life care in patients' homes, funded mainly by Medicare. It is private, owned by Clayton, Dubilier and Rice, and combined with Kindred at Home. Funding of $900 million is shown. Healthcare services provider with limited brand awareness outside its sector.

Geron is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Foster City, California, and listed on Nasdaq (GERN). Its product Rytelo (imetelstat), a telomerase inhibitor approved by the FDA in June 2024, treats lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) with transfusion-dependent anaemia, and is sold to haematologists in the US, with a European launch. Revenue is early stage, with funding of about $1 billion shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

iHeartMedia is the largest US radio broadcaster, with roughly 850 stations, listed on Nasdaq (IHRT) and run from a base in San Antonio with a New York presence. It owns the iHeartRadio streaming app, a large podcast network, Premiere Networks syndication, and live events including the iHeartRadio Music Festival and Jingle Ball, and sells advertising to national and local brands. It reaches over 90% of Americans monthly, with revenue of about $3.8 billion. Strong consumer media brand.

Janux Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (JANX). It develops tumour-activated T cell engagers using its TRACTr and TRACIr platforms, with lead programmes JANX007 for prostate cancer and JANX008 for solid tumours. It has no approved products and earns small collaboration revenue. Total funding of about $900 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

LANXESS is a German specialty chemicals group based in Cologne, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, created in 2004 from Bayer's chemicals business. It makes additives, intermediates, flame retardants, lubricant additives and high-performance materials for automotive, construction, agriculture, water treatment and consumer end markets, with revenue of about 6.5 billion euros and some 13,000 employees. It holds naming rights to Cologne's LANXESS arena and has sponsored Borussia Dortmund. B2B brand with strong corporate recognition in Germany.

Medici Living Group is a Berlin-based real estate developer and operator of micro-living, student and co-living apartments, building and running furnished small apartments in German and European cities for students and young professionals. It earns rental income and development margins, and has raised large amounts of investor capital, with a funding total of about 1 billion shown for 2018. Customers are tenants and institutional investors. Consumer-facing for tenants but a niche brand.

NFP was a US insurance broker and consultant, based in New York, providing property and casualty, benefits, retirement and wealth management services to businesses and individuals through a network of advisers and acquired firms. It was founded in 1998 and was taken private by Madison Dearborn Partners in 2015. Aon acquired it in 2024 in a deal valued at about $13 billion. Customers are mid-market employers and wealthy families. B2B financial services brand with little consumer awareness.

Novocure is a Swiss-incorporated oncology device company, with operations in Baar, Switzerland, and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, listed on Nasdaq (NVCS). Its Optune system delivers Tumor Treating Fields, electrical fields applied through a wearable device on the patient's skin to slow cancer cell division, approved for glioblastoma and mesothelioma, with trials in pancreatic and lung cancers. Revenue is roughly $600 million with funding of about $1.1 billion. Known to oncologists and patients, with limited public brand awareness.

Ping An Good Doctor, now Ping An Health and Technology, is an online healthcare platform based in Shenzhen, part of Ping An Insurance Group and listed in Hong Kong. It offers online doctor consultations, family doctor services, health management, pharmacy delivery and hospital referrals to tens of millions of Chinese users and corporate and insurance clients. Funding of $900 million was raised in 2018. A well-known digital health brand in China tied to the Ping An group.

Rothesay is a UK pension insurance company based in London, specialising in buying out defined benefit pension schemes. It insures liabilities of tens of billions of pounds for several hundred thousand pensioners, taking on assets from corporate pension trustees and managing them with long-term investments. Owners include GIC, Blackstone and MassMutual. Customers are corporate pension funds. Highly regarded in the financial industry, with low consumer brand awareness.

Weipinhui, known internationally as Vipshop, is a Chinese online discount retailer based in Guangzhou and listed on the NYSE (VIPS), founded in 2008. It runs flash-sale style events offering branded apparel, shoes, cosmetics and home goods at discounts to tens of millions of active customers, with logistics operated in its own warehouses, and has partnerships with Tencent and JD.com. Revenue is around 15 billion dollars. Well known consumer brand in China.

Wirecard was a German payments and financial technology group based in Aschheim near Munich, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and a member of the DAX. It processed card payments and offered issuing services to merchants worldwide, particularly e-commerce clients. In June 2020 it admitted that about 1.9 billion euros were missing from its accounts, filed for insolvency, and its former chief executive Markus Braun was later charged with fraud. It no longer operates as a going concern. Once a high-profile fintech, now notorious.

Yonghui Superstores is a Chinese supermarket and fresh food retail chain, historically based in Fuzhou and now run from Shanghai, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601933). It operates hundreds of large-format hypermarkets and fresh stores across China, selling groceries, fresh produce and own-brand products, and has used partnerships with JD.com, Tencent and Dairy Farm. Customers are mass-market Chinese shoppers. Revenue is tens of billions of yuan, with losses in recent years. Familiar consumer retail brand in China.

Ankura is a US business advisory and expert services firm, with its main office in New York, offering consulting in disputes, investigations, cybersecurity, restructuring, risk and compliance, and other specialist areas. Clients are corporations, law firms, governments and private equity. Founded in 2014 and PE-backed, it grew through acquisitions to thousands of staff across many countries. Funding of about $810 million is shown. B2B professional services brand with low public awareness.

AtaiBeckley is a US biopharmaceutical company based in New York, listed on Nasdaq (ATAI), formed by the combination of atai Life Sciences and Beckley Psytech in 2025. It develops short-acting psychedelic-derived treatments for mental health disorders, including mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) for depression and DMT-based programmes. It is clinical stage with no revenue from products and total funding of about $800 million. Known to investors in the psychedelics sector, with no consumer profile.

Briggs and Stratton is a US maker of small gasoline engines and outdoor power equipment, based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, founded in 1908. Widely recognised consumer-industrial brand in North America.

Certara is a US biosimulation software and technology-enabled services company based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, and listed on Nasdaq (CERT). Customers include most of the large pharma companies and the FDA. Revenue is about 400 million dollars. B2B scientific software brand with no consumer awareness.

CF Industries Holdings is a US nitrogen fertiliser producer based in Northbrook, Illinois, and listed on the NYSE (CF). Revenue is around $6 billion to $7 billion. B2B commodity producer with strong recognition among growers, none among consumers.

Edgewise Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Boulder, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (EWTX). Total funding of about $740 million is shown. Specialist biotech known to investors and patient communities, with no consumer brand profile.

EyePoint Pharmaceuticals is a US ophthalmology biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (EYPT). It specialises in sustained-release eye implants, with marketed products such as Yutiq and its lead development drug Duravyu (vorolanib) for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease, designed to cut the number of injections patients need. Customers are retina specialists. Funding of about $800 million is shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

Fulcrum Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (FULC). It focuses on rare genetic diseases, with its lead programme pociredir, an oral drug to raise fetal haemoglobin in sickle cell disease. An earlier muscular dystrophy programme, losmapimod, did not succeed in trials. It has no approved products and relies on investor funding, with about $778 million raised. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Impulse Dynamics is a medical device company based in Marlton, New Jersey, with its roots in Israel and Germany. Its Optimizer Smart System is an implantable device delivering cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) therapy for patients with heart failure, sold to cardiologists and hospitals in the US, Europe and elsewhere. It is privately held with venture backing and has raised nearly $700 million in total. Specialist cardiac device maker with no consumer brand profile.

Inari is a US agricultural biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 and backed by Flagship Pioneering. It uses gene editing and data science to design seeds with higher yields and lower input needs, starting with soybeans and corn, and plans to license or sell seed to farmers through partners and seed distributors. It is privately held and has raised around $750 million. B2B seed technology firm with little public brand awareness.

Invivyd is a US biopharmaceutical company, formerly Adagio Therapeutics, with its operations in the Boston area and a New Haven link in the data, listed on Nasdaq (IVVD). It develops monoclonal antibodies against COVID-19 and respiratory viruses, and its Pemgarda (pemivibart) received emergency use authorisation in 2024 as pre-exposure prophylaxis for immunocompromised patients. Customers are hospitals, infusion centres and pharmacies. Total funding is about $680 million. Specialist biotech with limited consumer awareness.

KalVista Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company based in Framingham, Massachusetts, with research in Salisbury, UK, and listed on Nasdaq (KALV). Its product sebetralstat (Ekterly), approved by the FDA in 2025, is the first oral on-demand treatment for hereditary angioedema attacks, sold to specialist physicians and patients. Funding of about $820 million is shown. Specialist pharma that is moving from development to commercial stage, with no general consumer awareness.

LetsGetChecked is a health technology company founded in Ireland in 2014 and based in New York, offering at-home diagnostic test kits that people mail to labs for results. Its tests cover sexually transmitted infections, hormones, cholesterol, vitamin levels and cancer screening, with prescriptions and clinical follow-up, sold to consumers online and via employers and health systems in the US, UK and Ireland. It is privately held and has raised about $700 million. Known as a direct-to-consumer health brand with advertising.

Nephron Pharmaceuticals is a family-owned US pharmaceutical manufacturer, headquartered in the Southeast, producing sterile prefilled syringes, outsourcing-facility injectable medicines for hospitals, and respiratory products such as inhalation solutions. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and healthcare distributors. It is one of the larger private 503B outsourcing manufacturers. The funding figure of about $775 million appears to be debt or facility financing. B2B healthcare manufacturer with little public brand awareness.

Novotech is a contract research organisation, started in Sydney and now with headquarters in Singapore, that runs clinical trials for biotech and pharma companies across Asia-Pacific, the US and Europe. It offers trial design, regulatory, site management and data services, and says it is the largest regional CRO in Asia Pacific. It is backed by private equity investors, including TPG. Funding of $760 million is shown, dated March 2025. B2B services provider with no consumer visibility.

Nurix Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Francisco, listed on Nasdaq (NRIX), working on targeted protein degradation. Its lead drug bexobrutideg degrades BTK for B-cell cancers, and it has partnerships with Sanofi, Pfizer and Gilead, using its DELigase platform. It has no approved products and earns collaboration revenue. Funding of about $796 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Olema Oncology is a US clinical-stage oncology company based in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (OLMA). Its lead drug palazestrant is an oral estrogen receptor antagonist being tested in Phase 3 for ER-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, alone and with CDK4/6 inhibitors. It has no approved products. Funding of about $765 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Precigen is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Germantown, Maryland, listed on Nasdaq (PGEN). It develops gene and cell therapies, with its lead product PRGN-2012 targeting recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, a rare airway disease caused by HPV. It was formerly Intrexon and once owned many synthetic biology holdings, which it has sold off, such as Trans Ova Genetics. Funding of about $810 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Qiagen is a molecular diagnostics and sample preparation company, legally based in Venlo, Netherlands, with major operations in Hilden, Germany, and Germantown, Maryland. It is listed on the NYSE and Frankfurt (QGEN). It sells kits and instruments to extract and test DNA and RNA, such as QuantiFERON-TB tests, QIAstat-Dx syndromic panels and bioinformatics software, to hospitals, labs, pharma and researchers worldwide. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. B2B brand well known in labs, not to consumers.

Rapt Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (RAPT). It develops oral and injectable drugs for inflammatory and allergic diseases, including an anti-IgE antibody candidate for food allergy and asthma. An earlier oral CCR4 programme for cancer was discontinued. It has no approved product, with about $840 million raised. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Selina is a hospitality brand based in London that runs hostels, hotels, co-working spaces and experience offerings for digital nomads and young travellers, with properties across Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere. It went public on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger in 2022. Customers are budget and mid-range travellers, and revenue comes from rooms, food, beverage and co-working memberships. Founded in 2014, it has had heavy losses. Consumer brand with some recognition among backpackers and remote workers.

Windtree Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Warrington, Pennsylvania, listed on Nasdaq. It develops istaroxime, an intravenous drug for acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock, and has had financial difficulties and several restructurings. It has no approved products or meaningful revenue. Funding of about $733 million appears in the data. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

X4 Pharmaceuticals is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Boston and listed on Nasdaq (XFOR). Its product Xolremdi (mavorixafor), approved by the FDA in April 2024, treats WHIM syndrome, a rare inherited immune disorder, and is being tested in chronic neutropenia. Customers are immunologists and rare disease patients. Funding of about $760 million is shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Acadia Healthcare is a US behavioural health provider based in Franklin, Tennessee, and listed on Nasdaq (ACHC). It is the largest standalone operator of psychiatric hospitals and addiction treatment centres in the country, with roughly 250 to 260 facilities and some 10,000 beds. Revenue is about 3 billion dollars, mostly from Medicare, Medicaid and insurers. It has been through legal scrutiny of admission practices. Healthcare provider brand with limited consumer awareness.

Alltech is a private animal health and nutrition company based in Nicholasville, Kentucky, founded in 1980 by Dr Pearse Lyons. It makes feed supplements, yeast products and mineral nutrition for livestock and pets, with operations in over 100 countries, and runs the Lexington Brewing and Distilling Company producing Kentucky Ale and Town Branch bourbon. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. It was title sponsor of the FEI World Equestrian Games in 2010 and 2018. B2B brand with some consumer-facing drinks and equestrian profile.

Belite Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, listed on Nasdaq (BLTE), with research ties to Taiwan. Its lead drug tinlarebant is an oral therapy to reduce vitamin A dimer build-up in the eye, in trials for Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration. It has no approved products. Funding of about $589 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

C4 Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (CCCC). It develops targeted protein degradation drugs, using its TORPEDO platform to destroy disease-causing proteins, with candidates such as cemsidomide for blood cancers, and collaborations with Roche, Biogen and Merck KGaA. It has no approved products and earns partnership revenue. Funding of about $574 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Evolus is a US medical aesthetics company based in Newport Beach, California, and listed on Nasdaq (EOLS). It markets Jeuveau (prabotulinumtoxinA), a botulinum toxin competing with Botox for frown lines, and, from 2024, the Evolysse range of hyaluronic acid fillers, selling to aesthetic physicians in the US, Europe and Canada. Its Jeuveau is made by South Korea's Daewoong. Revenue is about 270 million dollars. Branded to consumers through marketing campaigns, so it has moderate public awareness.

Insulet is a US medical device company based in Acton, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (PODD). Its Omnipod system is a tubeless, wearable insulin pump with an automated insulin delivery algorithm for people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, sold through pharmacies and distributors in the US and about two dozen other countries. Revenue is around 2 billion dollars and growing. Strong brand among people with diabetes and clinicians, with growing consumer recognition.

Ipsen is a French specialty biopharmaceutical group based in Paris, listed on Euronext Paris and controlled by the Beaufour family. It sells Dysport (botulinum toxin), Somatuline, Onivyde and Cabometyx outside the US, and rare disease drugs such as Bylvay, in oncology, neuroscience and rare diseases, in more than 100 countries. Revenue is about 3 billion euros with roughly 5,000 employees. B2B pharma with strong standing among physicians and limited public awareness.

Jubilant Bhartia Group is an Indian conglomerate based in Noida, led by Shyam and Hari Bhartia. Its holdings include Jubilant FoodWorks, the master franchisee of Domino's Pizza in India and also Dunkin' and other restaurant brands, Jubilant Pharmova (pharma and radiopharmacy), Jubilant Ingrevia (specialty chemicals) and Jubilant Agri. The group has multiple listed companies and revenue in the billions of dollars. Domino's India gives it strong consumer recognition.

Lyell Immunopharma is a US clinical-stage cell therapy company based in South San Francisco, listed on Nasdaq (LYEL). It develops CAR-T cell therapies for solid and blood cancers, led by rondecabtagene autoleucel (ronde-cel) for large B-cell lymphoma, using its own cell manufacturing capability. It has no approved product. Funding of about $593 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Oculis is a Swiss biopharmaceutical company, with offices in Zug and a Lausanne link, listed on Nasdaq (OCS) and Iceland. It develops eye medicines, including OCS-01 eye drops for diabetic macular oedema, OCS-02 for dry eye and the neuro-ophthalmology candidate privosegtor, aiming to replace injections with topical treatments. It has no approved product yet. Funding of about $619 million is shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Prime Medicine is a US gene editing company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (PRME). It develops prime editing, a technology invented in the lab of Harvard's David Liu that can rewrite DNA letters without cutting both strands, targeting genetic diseases such as chronic granulomatous disease and liver disorders. It is partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb on cell therapies. It has no approved product. Funding of about $558 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Samunnati is an Indian agri-value-chain finance and services company based in Chennai, founded in 2014.
