It is privately held and backed by investors including Dutch and impact funds. Funding of about $560 million is shown. B2B agri-finance brand with little consumer visibility.

Soleno Therapeutics is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Redwood City, California, and listed on Nasdaq (SLNO). Its product Vykat XR (diazoxide choline), approved by the FDA in 2025, treats hyperphagia (constant hunger) in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome, a rare genetic disorder, and is sold through specialty pharmacies. Funding of about $569 million is shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

Tubulis is a German biotechnology company based in Munich that develops antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancer, using its Tub-tag and P5 conjugation technologies to attach toxins to antibodies. Its lead programmes target solid tumours such as ovarian and lung cancer and are in clinical trials. It is privately held and venture backed, with funding of about 544 million shown for late 2025. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

Volta Charging was a US electric vehicle charging network operator, with offices in San Francisco and Los Angeles, that offered free charging at shopping centres and retail sites, funded by advertising on screens built into its stations. It listed on the NYSE through a SPAC merger in 2021 and was acquired by Shell in early 2023 for about 169 million dollars. Customers were EV drivers, site hosts and advertisers. The brand now sits within Shell's EV charging business.

Wilbur-Ellis is a US agribusiness, chemical and feed distribution company, privately held and employee-owned, founded in 1921. It markets crop protection products, seed, fertiliser and specialty ingredients to farmers and growers, supplies animal feed and ingredients, and its Connell Company handles trading in Asia and elsewhere. It operates across North America, Asia-Pacific and other regions, with revenue of about 4 to 5 billion dollars. B2B brand strongly known among growers, with little consumer awareness.

Ynsect was a French insect protein producer based in Paris, which farmed mealworms to make protein and oil for animal feed, pet food and fertiliser, with a large vertical farm called Ynfarm near Amiens. It raised more than 500 million dollars from investors and became one of the biggest insect-farming ventures worldwide. The company entered insolvency proceedings in 2025 and has largely wound down. Customers were feed and pet food makers. B2B agritech with little consumer awareness.

Altera Infrastructure, formerly Teekay Offshore, is a Bermuda-registered offshore energy services company based in Hamilton, owned by Brookfield. It owns and operates shuttle tankers, floating production storage and offloading units (FPSOs), floating storage units and towage vessels for oil companies, especially in the North Sea and Brazil. It restructured through a Chapter 11 process in 2022. Customers are oil majors and national oil companies. B2B maritime energy business with no consumer visibility.

CMPC is a Chilean forestry, pulp, paper, packaging and tissue company based in Santiago and listed on the Santiago Stock Exchange, controlled by the Matte family. It produces eucalyptus and pine pulp, containerboard and corrugated packaging, and consumer tissue and diapers under brands such as Elite, Confort and Babysec in Latin America. Revenue is about 7 to 8 billion dollars. B2B pulp and packaging, plus consumer hygiene brands that are very visible across Chile and Latin America.

It is a mid-sized component supplier that has been through industry price pressure and consolidation. B2B component maker with no consumer brand awareness.

National Tobacco Enterprise (NTE) is Ethiopia's main cigarette maker, based in Addis Ababa, which was state-owned until Japan Tobacco International bought a 51% stake in 2016 for about 510 million dollars, the funding figure shown here. It makes and distributes cigarette brands such as Gisha, Nyala and Crown to Ethiopian consumers and wholesalers. Ethiopia's government kept the remaining share. Consumer brands are well known locally, though tobacco sponsorship is heavily restricted.

Oceanwide Expeditions is a Dutch expedition cruise operator based in Vlissingen, Zeeland, founded in 1993, running small-ship voyages to Antarctica, the Arctic, Greenland, Spitsbergen and sub-Antarctic islands. Funding of about 443 million is shown for 2020. Niche travel brand with strong recognition among polar travellers.

Tecnoglass is a Colombian manufacturer of architectural glass, windows and aluminium products, based in Barranquilla and listed on the NYSE (TGLS). It supplies tempered, laminated and insulated glass, window and curtain wall systems for commercial and residential buildings, with most sales in the US, especially Florida. Founded by the Daes family, it has revenue of about 800 to 900 million dollars. B2B building products brand with little consumer awareness.

Telia Company is a Nordic and Baltic telecom group based in Solna, near Stockholm, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and Helsinki, with the Swedish state as its largest owner. It provides mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise services in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia, with about 20 million subscriptions and revenue of around 85 billion kronor. It has a long record of sports and cultural sponsorship in the region. Strong consumer brand across the Nordics and Baltics.

Akropolis is a Baltic retail property developer and operator based in Vilnius, Lithuania, running the Akropolis shopping and entertainment centres in Vilnius, Klaipeda, Siauliai and Latvia, with cinemas, ice rinks, shops and restaurants. Well known consumer destination brand in Lithuania.

Circulus is a US plastics recycling company based in Ardmore, Oklahoma, that turns used polyolefin plastics such as polyethylene and polypropylene into post-consumer recycled resins for packaging and consumer goods makers. B2B sustainability materials supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Codemao is a Chinese children's coding and programming education company based in Shenzhen. Revenue comes from course fees paid by parents and from hardware and school sales. It has raised about 450 million dollars, with a Hong Kong listing in recent years. Known among parents in China as an edtech brand.

iSpot.tv is a US TV advertising measurement and analytics company based in Bellevue, near Seattle, founded in 2012. Customers are brands, agencies and media companies, and it is privately held with about 380 million dollars raised. B2B ad tech brand with low public awareness, but well known among marketers.

Marimaca Copper is a Chilean-focused copper exploration and development company, headquartered in Santiago and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and ASX. Its Marimaca Oxide Deposit is in the Antofagasta region of northern Chile, planned as an open-pit, heap-leach and solvent extraction-electrowinning operation producing copper cathode, with a larger sulphide resource below. It has no revenue yet. Funding of about 417 million dollars is shown for 2026. Resource developer with no consumer brand visibility.

Customers are publishers and brands. It is privately held and has raised about 393 million dollars. B2B media technology brand, well known in publishing, with little consumer awareness.

Tyco Electronics Group was the electronic components business spun out of Tyco International in 2007, now known as TE Connectivity (NYSE: TEL). Accendra Health is the name taken by the home-based healthcare business of Owens and Minor after that group sold its products and healthcare services unit. Customers are patients at home, referred by physicians and paid by insurers and Medicare. Funding of $326 million is shown for 2026. Healthcare brand with some consumer recognition, mainly among patients.

Aidacare is an Australian provider of medical equipment and home care products, based in Sydney, supplying mobility aids, hospital beds, pressure care cushions, respiratory and daily living products to individuals, hospitals, aged care homes and government schemes such as the NDIS. It sells through retail stores, online, and service contracts. It is privately held with investor backing. Funding of about 540 million Australian dollars is shown for 2026. Known to Australian carers and patients, though not a mass-market consumer brand.

Amaroq Minerals is a Greenland-focused mining exploration and development company with its corporate office in Toronto, Canada, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, AIM and Nasdaq Iceland. It is run from a Nuuk and Reykjavik base, and has raised about 344 million dollars. Resource company with no consumer brand visibility.

Americas Gold and Silver is a Toronto-based precious metals mining company, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and NYSE American (USAS). It operates the Galena Complex in Idaho and the Cosala operations in Sinaloa, Mexico, producing silver, gold, lead and zinc concentrate, and has a stake in the Relief Canyon project in Nevada. Customers are smelters and traders. Revenue is around 100 to 200 million dollars. Mining company with no consumer brand profile.

Cirba Solutions is a US battery recycling and critical materials company, with its main office in North Carolina, formed in 2021 by the combination of Retriev Technologies and Heritage Battery Recycling. It collects end-of-life and scrap lithium-ion batteries, recycles them at facilities in Ohio, South Carolina and Nevada, and supplies black mass and recovered metals to battery material producers. Customers are automakers, battery makers and manufacturers. Funding of 377 million dollars is shown. B2B sustainability firm with low public awareness.

Civeo Corporation is a Houston-based provider of workforce accommodation, with large lodges for oil sands, mining and infrastructure workers in Canada and Australia, listed on the NYSE (CVEO). It rents beds in remote villages and offers catering, housekeeping and facility management, and sells to resource companies and contractors. Revenue is around 700 million dollars. It was spun out of Oil States International in 2014. B2B hospitality-style services business with no consumer brand profile.

Cleveland Clinic is a US non-profit academic medical centre based in Cleveland, Ohio, founded in 1921. It runs a main campus and regional hospitals in Ohio and Florida, with international sites in Abu Dhabi, London and Toronto, offering specialist care in cardiac, neurological, digestive and other fields, with about 80,000 caregivers and revenue of around 15 billion dollars. It is a major sports partner of Cleveland teams. Highly recognised healthcare brand in the US.

CSG International (CSG Systems) is a US software and services company based in Englewood, Colorado, listed on Nasdaq (CSGS). It provides billing, customer experience, monetisation and digital payments software, largely SaaS, to telecom operators, cable and media companies, plus businesses in other industries, including Charter and Comcast as big customers. Revenue is about 1.2 billion dollars. B2B technology brand with little public awareness, though large communications clients.

It builds a search engine and API designed for AI applications, letting developers and AI agents retrieve relevant web content using neural embeddings and natural-language queries. B2B developer tool with strong standing among AI engineers and no consumer brand awareness.

Fairino is a Chinese robotics company based in Suzhou, Jiangsu, that designs and sells collaborative industrial robots and related control software and components. B2B automation brand with no consumer awareness.

Graphite One Resources is a Canadian mining and advanced materials company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, with a corporate office in Vancouver and ties to Calgary. It is developing the Graphite Creek deposit near Nome, Alaska, one of the largest known graphite resources in the US, together with a planned battery anode material plant in Ohio, supported by US government funding. It has no production yet and has raised about 349 million dollars. Resource developer with no consumer brand profile.

Grow Therapy is a US mental health platform based in New York, founded in 2020, that connects people with therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their health insurance, including video sessions. It offers practice tools to therapists for billing, scheduling and credentialing. Patients are consumers across most US states, and it has raised more than 300 million dollars, including 2026 funding. It has meaningful consumer advertising, with strong awareness in the mental health space.

Impress is a Spanish orthodontic technology company based in Barcelona that makes clear aligners and sells treatment plans through partner dentists and orthodontists, as an alternative to Invisalign, with some direct-to-consumer marketing.
